82108.subject: Weekly Recap: Binance Reopens as Its Hackers Keep Moving Funds
82108.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

**Binance** spent the week reopening withdrawals and explaining how attackers took $6.34 billion, while the attackers kept converting what Binance could not freeze. **Democrats** won both chambers of Congress, and by our count the CLARITY Act is still 11 votes short of ending debate in the Senate.

Security incidents kept landing on infrastructure. A Linux kernel flaw kept **Threshold**'s tBTC bridge offline all week, a **reth** client bug led vaults and bridges to pause, and **Gnosis Pay** confirmed a breach that exposed card customers' home addresses and wallet addresses. **Polygon** validators were asked to approve a hard fork that would hand stolen POL back to its owners.

Enjoy!

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### WATCH

## THORChain Refused to Block the $387M Bitget Hacker. Here’s Why | Chad Barraford

Youtube: THORChain Refused to Block the $387M Bitget Hacker. Here’s Why | Chad Barraford (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5i3zElaKxc)

**Chad Barraford**, THORChain's technical co-founder, explains why THORChain did not block the hacker behind Bitget's $387 million theft. The FBI has since asked THORChain node operators to block funds from the Binance hack, and this week the attackers swapped XRP into bitcoin through THORChain. [**Listen to the episode.**](https://thedefiant.io/news/podcast/thorchain-refused-to-block-the-usd387m-bitget-hacker-here-s-why-or-chad-barraford)

———————————————————————————

# Top Stories This Week

## Binance Reopens Withdrawals and Traces Its Hack to a Fake Job Interview

Binance [began reopening withdrawals](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-begins-reopening-withdrawals-with-bitcoin-after-6-3-billion-hack) on Sunday, starting with bitcoin, and its tracked wallets [posted a $4.54 billion net outflow](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-posts-4-54-billion-net-outflow-as-tracked-rivals-gain-564-million) in the first hours. On Tuesday, a [technical report](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-details-months-long-campaign-behind-6-34-billion-hack) traced the theft to a fake job interview in September. Malware from a coding assignment let the attackers reach Binance's wallet-signing service, which signed an EIP-7702 delegation that let an outside contract empty a hot wallet. By our arithmetic, Binance cleared that delegation 3 hours and 46 minutes after the first sweep. It put the funds frozen or intercepted at about $2.85 billion, and its wallets [swung back to net inflows](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/binance-flips-to-1-82-billion-in-daily-net-inflows-after-withdrawal-restart). On Wednesday, Binance [widened its proof of reserves to 44 tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-expands-proof-of-reserves-to-44-tokens-after-hack) and said it had replaced about 98% of the stolen assets, and THORChain [restarted most swaps](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/thorchain-restarts-most-swaps-with-14-nodes-yet-to-upgrade).
